tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Complete partial limits are geometric limits] ↗ def:geometric-limit

Suppose that $(U_k,g_k,x_k)$ is a sequence of based Riemannian manifolds and that there is a partial geometric limit $(U_\infty ,g_\infty ,x_\infty )$ that is a complete Riemannian manifold. Then this partial geometric limit is a geometric limit.

Proof

\sketch ↗ def:geometric-limit ↗ def:delta-regular-point Since the balls $B(x_\infty ,R)$ have compact closure in $U_\infty $ and since

\[ \operatorname {Reg}_\delta (U_\infty ,g_\infty ,x_\infty )=U_\infty \]

for every $\delta >0$, it is easy to see that the extra condition, (2b), in Definition 1 is automatic in this case.

□

Theorem
[Geometric convergence for complete manifolds]
